next_step: Closed-lost review; collect POC logs for RCA; follow-up in 3 months if budget reopens
notes:
Account overview:
- Sable Horizon Commerce — mid-sized e-commerce platform (marketplace + first-party catalogue). Heavy on order/checkout automation and post-purchase workflows.
- Looking for reliable structured outputs (JSON order objects), deterministic tool-calling for payment/fulfillment hooks, and guaranteed audit logs.
Why stalled / closed-lost (summary):
- POC surfaced a quality regression vs their incumbent (IncumbentVendorX) on structured outputs and tool-calls. Redwood prototype produced malformed JSON in 2 of 8 flows and missed required fields in line items -> downstream order failures in their sandbox.
- Security team escalated: inability to prove deterministic schema adherence + missing fine-grained audit trails for tool invocations = blocker for production.
- Budget freeze announced by CFO during procurement cycle; internal champion (Head of AI, Lina Torres) left to competitor in late Jan. No replacement sponsor.
Key quotes from stakeholders:
- "We can't risk inventory mismatches in peak season — the incumbent guarantees schema conformity." (VP Ops)
- "Hallucinated SKUs and a dropped shipping_address field broke our downstream ledger; we need 100% schema pass rate for production." (Platform Eng)
Timeline (short, CRM style):
- 2025-11-06: Intro call (AE Riley Chen) — high intent, need for deterministic outputs.
- 2025-11-18: Tech deep-dive w/ SE (Jamal) — agreed on POC scope (catalog -> checkout -> fulfillment hook).
- 2025-12-01: POC kickoff — provided sample catalog + test harness.
- 2025-12-10: Recording ff_2025-12-10-9854 — initial demo; Redwood generated expected outputs but with some schema drift.
- 2026-01-08: POC milestone: 50k test tokens; found 2 failing flows (malformed JSON, missing required fields). Logged RDW-1824.
- 2026-01-22: Security review call (ff_2026-01-22-1102) — security rejected until schema/fallback guarantees + audit logs are demonstrable.
- 2026-02-05: Pricing push from incumbent; Sable's procurement requests 12-mo committed discount. CFO announces budget hold.
- 2026-02-18: Final sync; champion left for competitor; decision to pause procurement.
Outcomes and rationale for loss:
- Lost to IncumbentVendorX: they offered a short-term price + contractual schema validation SLA; incumbent also had a pre-built adapter to Sable's fulfillment system.
- Primary technical reason: quality regression in structured output and unreliable tool-calling semantics vs incumbent baseline. Secondary: security/audit expectations not met in current POC artifacts.
Open follow-ups (internal):
- Collect POC logs, payload diffs, and failing examples for RCA (SE + runtime). Ticketed RDW-1978 for reproducibility.
- Post-mortem: document root cause (kernel selection/path causing tokenization drift on certain SKU strings) and mitigation (schema validator wrapper, stricter sampling/beam settings, runtime deterministic mode).
- Sales action: mark as closed-lost; schedule 90-day nurture cadence and product update ping if schema guarantees feature ships.
Next visible risks if re-engaged:
- Without a deterministic structured-output mode and auditable tool-call chain Redwood will not meet procurement/security bar.
